thread:
sara: FYI customer on private VPC reports invoice token count ~3x the dashboard for Feb. They run the onprem meter-agent and also publish audit logs. Can we triage?

devon: which customer / which deployment? any recent infra maintenance windows? :eyes:

sara: ACME-Health, VPC in eu-west-1. Customer says agent restarted during a scheduled infra maint on 2026-03-03 02:00 UTC. Dashboard shows 1.2M tokens, invoice 3.6M. Audit logs (they attached) show many offline buffering events and a few ``queue dropped`` entries.

ashok: can you paste the agent version and config? busy windows + restart could cause replay duplicates if seq ids reset or replay logic double-submits.

sara: agent version 1.8.2, config snippet they sent: ``metering:
  mode: offline-buffering
  max_buffer_mb: 512
  replay_policy: best_effort
  seqid_persist: /var/lib/redwood/seqid.db``

kevin: best_effort replay shouldn't duplicate, but if seqid_persist got cleared on restart we could see duplicates. do they have the agent journal or last bytes of ``seqid.db``? any log lines like ``replayed N events``?

sara: logs show: ``2026-03-03T02:01:12Z INFO buffer flush triggered (window=30s)`` then ``2026-03-03T02:01:15Z ERROR queue overflow, dropping 112 events`` then ``2026-03-03T02:01:17Z INFO replay started, 421 events`` and later ``2026-03-03T02:01:19Z INFO replay finished, acked 421``. They also have audit ledger showing 842 acked events around that time.

devon: hmm ledger shows 842 acked but meter backend only shows 421 accepted? or other way around? which direction is mismatch?

sara: invoice counts are higher than dashboard/accepted calls. Their audit ledger is higher than our ingestion in some windows.

ashok: two hypotheses: 1) agent double-acked during replay due to clock skew/incorrect monotonic sequence check; 2) ingestion path accepted duplicates (replayed events with new unique IDs) and dedupe didn't trigger because header seqid changed. Need specific request/response traces.

kevin: ask customer for a short repro: export the agent logs around the window and run this locally: ``sqlite3 /var/lib/redwood/seqid.db 'select * from seq_offsets order by ts desc limit 20;'`` also ``jq .events | jq -r '.[].seqid' | sort | uniq -c`` on the replay file if they have it.

sara: asked them for those commands. They ran ``xxd -l 64 /var/lib/redwood/seqid.db`` and paste below.

meter-agent-bot: AUTOREPLY: please paste the full replay tarball using the secure upload link: https://files.redwood.example/s/xyz (expires in 1h).

devon: also ask them to run ``date -u && sudo chronyc tracking`` to show NTP/chrony status. If clock jumped forward/back during replay, timestamps used for dedupe TTL could behave oddly.

sara: they ran chrony: ``Leap status: Normal
Reference ID: 10.0.0.5
Stratum 2
Last offset : -0.0032s``. No obvious huge jump but the system clock log shows a ``kernel: time_adjust: 35400s step`` around 02:00 UTC (syslog snippet).

ashok: that kernel time step is huge (9.83 hours). That explains a lot — if the agent uses wall-clock timestamps for dedupe window or for generating replay batch ids and the clock was stepped, replay ack timestamps may land outside expected windows causing ledger vs ingestion mismatch.

kevin: next steps: 1) confirm whether seqid.db persisted across restart or got recreated (compare inode / file size pre/post). 2) compute overlap between audit events and ingestion accepted IDs to see duplicates. Ask customer to run our audit tool: ``/usr/local/bin/rw-meter-audit --from 2026-03-03T01:55Z --to 2026-03-03T02:10Z --out replay-events.ndjson`` then run ``jq -s 'flatten | map(.seqid) | group_by(.) | map({seqid: .[0], count: length})' replay-events.ndjson | jq .[] | sort -r -k2``

sara: they provided the replay-events.ndjson. Quick scan shows some seqids repeated twice in short bursts, often right after the time step.

devon: ok that nails it — clock step + agent restart -> seqid persistence may have been lost -> replay created overlapping seqids or re-issued events with new ids but duplicated tokens. We should verify whether the ingestion path dedup key is (customer_id, seqid) or (request_id) and whether replay assigns new request_ids.

ashok: I can check backend logs for dedupe key behavior. Kevin, can you grep ingestion logs for ACME-Health around 02:01 and show any 409/duplicate responses? pattern: ``grep -E \"ACME-Health.*(duplicate|already seen|409)\" /var/log/redwood/ingest/*.log``

kevin: running now — found 37 lines: some ``duplicate event: seqid=...`` and others show ``accepted replayed event id=...``. So looks like a mix: a subset deduped, some got accepted. That would lead to higher invoice if accepted ones count tokens again.

sara: customer asked for mitigation — they want corrective action and invoice adjustment request.

devon: mitigation: 1) stop agent replay, patch agent to detect large kernel time steps and pause replay + mark for manual review. 2) backfill dedupe map in ingestion for the affected window by using audit ledger to mark accepted seqids, then recalc billing for that window. We should escalate to billing ops for adjustment.

ashok: I'll open a ticket with backend infra to run a dedupe reconciliation job for ACME-Health for 2026-03-03 01:50-02:15 UTC. Include the audit events tarball for authoritative count.

kevin: I'll prepare a quick patch to agent to make seqid persistence atomic (write-then-rename) and guard replays when clock jumps >1s. Add a metric ``meter.agent.replay_clock_jumps`` so we can alert.

meter-agent-bot: ACTION: created internal ticket INF-4982 for dedupe reconciliation and BILL-2210 for invoice review.

sara: thanks team — I'll coordinate with the customer on holding invoices and will post updates here once ops completes the reconciliation. :thumbsup:

devon: great. once ops runs job, we'll compare dashboard token totals vs ledger and send an adjusted statement.

ashok: note for postmortem: agent should treat monotonic clock for seqid timestamps. also add a startup check to refuse to start if seqid.db missing unless explicitly forced.

kevin: agreed. I'll put a draft patch PR and link it here when ready.

sara: customer is appreciative. closing loop soon.
